annotations.target_phrase: wills gen wonts, oystrygods gaggin fishygods
annotations.annotation_text: The primordial clash between the Ostrogoths and Visigoths (East and West Germanic tribes), transposed into Oyster-gods versus Fish-gods and theological antinomies between free will and predestined necessity.
sources: Gibbon, Edward. The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/25717
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://jhupbooks.press.jhu.edu/title/annotations-finnegans-wake

annotations.target_phrase: Brekkek Kekkek Kekkek Kekkek! Koax Koax Koax!
annotations.annotation_text: Direct transliteration of the croaking chorus of the frogs from Aristophanes's ancient Athenian comedy "The Frogs" (lines 209-210), chanted as Dionysus crosses the Acherusian lake to Hades.
sources: Aristophanes. The Frogs (trans. Benjamin Bickley Rogers). https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/7998

annotations.target_phrase: Ualu Ualu Ualu! Quaouauh!
annotations.annotation_text: Sounds of weeping, battle cries, and lamentations: Gaelic "ual" (wailing, keening) combined with Gaelic wolf-cries and the croaks of marsh-dwellers.
sources: O'Hehir, Brendan. A Gaelic Lexicon for Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/gaeliclexiconfor0000oheh

annotations.target_phrase: Baddelaries partisans are still out to mathmaster Malachus Micgranes
annotations.annotation_text: Historical Dublin feuds: the Batchelors and the Vances; also Malachi MacGrath and the Battle of Clontarf (1014). Blends with mathematical mastery and faction-fighting.
sources: Curtis, Edmund. A History of Ireland. https://archive.org/details/historyofireland0000curt

annotations.target_phrase: Verdons catapelting the camibalistics out of the Whoyteboyce of Hoodie Head
annotations.annotation_text: The Verdons and the Whiteboys (agrarian 18th-century Irish secret society in white smocks), with Howth Head ("Hoodie Head") as the battle site; cannibalistic catapulting.
sources: Lecky, W.E.H. A History of Ireland in the Eighteenth Century. https://archive.org/details/historyofireland01leckuoft

annotations.target_phrase: Assiegates and boomeringstroms
annotations.annotation_text: Warfare implements: fuses Zulu assagais (spears), Australian aboriginal boomerangs, and roaring maelstroms of conflict.
sources: Frazer, Sir James George. The Golden Bough. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/3623

annotations.target_phrase: Sanglorians, save! Arms apeal with larms, appalling
annotations.annotation_text: French "sang glorieux" (glorious blood) + St. Gloriana / Gloria in Excelsis; bells sounding alarms and calling to arms (bells pealing).
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp

annotations.target_phrase: cashels aired and ventilated
annotations.annotation_text: Irish "caiseal" (stone fort, stronghold), the Rock of Cashel, and castles aired and plundered.
sources: Joyce, P.W. The Origin and History of Irish Names of Places. https://archive.org/details/originandhistory01joycuoft

annotations.target_phrase: sinduced by what tegotetabsolvers
annotations.annotation_text: Fuses "sin-induced", seduction, and the confessional Latin "ego te absolvo" (I absolve thee) of Catholic priesthood.
sources: The Council of Trent: On the Sacrament of Penance. https://www.thelatinlibrary.com/trent.html

annotations.target_phrase: fanespanned most high heaven the skysign of soft advertisement
annotations.annotation_text: Spanning temples ("fanes") with the cosmic rainbow, which Joyce satirically envisions as a modern glowing neon sky-sign / commercial advertisement across the heavens.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish

annotations.target_phrase: But was iz? Iseut? Ere were sewers
annotations.annotation_text: Fuses Isolde / Iseult (Tristan's lover) with "Is it?" and Dublin's historical cloacae / drainage sewers, reflecting Dublin's underground waterways.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind

annotations.target_phrase: oaks of aid now they lie in peat yet elms leap where askes lay
annotations.annotation_text: Arboreal and resurrection motif: oak, elm, ash. The four sacred trees of ancient Ireland, fallen into the bog of peat but resurrecting out of the ashes (Phoenix).
sources: Frazer, Sir James George. The Golden Bough (The Worship of Trees). https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/3623

annotations.target_phrase: Phall if you but will, rise you must
annotations.annotation_text: The central moral and metaphysical axiom of Finnegans Wake: the Fall (Phall/phallus) is inevitable, but Resurrection (Viconian ricorso and rising) is mandatory.
sources: Vico, Giambattista. The New Science. https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/vico/
Ellmann, Richard. James Joyce. https://archive.org/details/jamesjoyce0000ellm

annotations.target_phrase: setdown secular phoenish
annotations.annotation_text: The Phoenix bird rising from its ashes; secular cycle of ages (Latin "saeculum"); Phoenix Park in Dublin; Finnish/Finnegan/finish.
sources: Ovid. Metamorphoses (Book XV: The Phoenix). https://www.thelatinlibrary.com/ovid/ovid.met15.shtml

annotations.target_phrase: Bygmester Finnegan, of the Stuttering Hand, freemen's maurer
annotations.annotation_text: Henrik Ibsen's master-builder Halvard Solness ("Bygmester Solness", 1892) fused with Tim Finnegan and Freemasonry (German "Maurer" = mason / builder). HCE's guilt manifest in a stuttering hand.
sources: Ibsen, Henrik. The Master Builder (Bygmester Solness). https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/4070
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe

annotations.target_phrase: joshuan judges had given us numbers or Helviticus committed deuteronomy
annotations.annotation_text: The Old Testament Pentateuch / Hexateuch: Joshua, Judges, Numbers, Leviticus ("Helviticus"), Deuteronomy, placing Finnegan's antiquity before scripture.
sources: The King James Bible: Pentateuch. https://www.biblegateway.com

annotations.target_phrase: man of hod, cement and edifices in Toper's Thorp piled buildung supra buildung
annotations.annotation_text: Finnegan the bricklayer with his hod, creating human civilization; German "Bildung" (culture/education) and "Gebäude" (building) over Toper's Thorp (Dublin: Baile Átha Cliath / town of drunkards).
sources: Mumford, Lewis. The City in History. https://archive.org/details/cityinhistoryits00mumf

annotations.target_phrase: livers by the Soangso
annotations.annotation_text: The dwellers by the River Liffey and the Chinese Hwang-Ho (Yellow River), universalizing rivers as the cradles of civilization.
sources: Hart, Clive. Structure and Motif in Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/structuremotifin0000hart

annotations.target_phrase: Haroun Childeric Eggeberth
annotations.annotation_text: HCE acronym: Harun al-Rashid (Abbasid Caliph of Arabian Nights), Childeric (Merovingian Frankish King), and Egbert (first Anglo-Saxon King of England).
sources: The Arabian Nights (trans. Sir Richard Burton). https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/3435

annotations.target_phrase: waalworth of a skyerscape of most eyeful hoyth entowerly
annotations.annotation_text: The Woolworth Building in New York (world's tallest skyscraper when built) merged with Howth Head and the Tower of Babel, reaching toward heaven.
sources: Genesis 11 (The Tower of Babel). https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+11&version=KJV
